title: Michoacán Tyrannosaurs, Raptors and ‘Duck-Billed’ Dinosaurs: Mexico Confirms Discovery of 50 Footprints in Apatzingán
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by La Jornada Editorial Staff originally appeared in the[October
26, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/26/ciencia-y-
tecnologia/tiranosaurios-raptores-y-dinosaurios-pico-de-pato-michoacanos-inah-
confirma-hallazgo-de-50-huellas-en-apatzingan), Mexico's premier left wing
daily newspaper._

The National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) reported the
discovery of **at least 50 fossilized dinosaur footprints** of various species
that inhabited part of the current territory of Apatzingán, Michoacán, 65
million years ago.

Among them, based on their morphology (size, shape, number of toes and depth),
they are attributed to three families of dinosaurs: a carnivorous one of
theropods, of large size, up to 4 meters tall, possibly that of the
**tyrannosaurids** , characterized by its three-toed footprint. Another
corresponds to smaller dinosaurs, up to 2 meters tall, similar to **raptors**
(Dromaeosauridae), with three toes; and an herbivorous one, of the **duck-
billed** type (Hadrosauridae), which could reach 4 meters in height, whose
footprint shows three toes with rounded ends.

![Researcher measuring a dinosaur footprint in
Apatzingán](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/apatzingan-dinosaur-tracks-02.jpg)The dimensions of
the ichnites range between 12 and 48 centimeters in length, and up to 30
centimeters in width. Photo: Centro INAH Michoacán

The dinosaur footprints were found in the bed of a stream, in the community of
San Juan de los Plátanos, municipality of Apatzingán. **The discovery began
with a notice from local residents** , who alerted the institute to the
presence of footprints of “giant animals.”

The researcher from the Centro INAH Michoacán, Raymundo Cervantes Barriga,
went to the site to make the assessment and confirmed that these are tracks of
herbivorous and carnivorous dinosaurs over an area of 40 square meters, on a
platform of sedimentary rock, at the edge of the river. The dimensions of the
ichnites range between 12 and 48 centimeters in length, and up to 30
centimeters in width.

Cervantes Barriga explains that these species lived 65 million years ago,
during the Late Cretaceous, when the region must have had bodies of water,
where the animals came to feed.

> A find of this kind opens a window onto a period that we all have in our
> imagination, but that we rarely get the opportunity to study.
>
> Archaeologist Punzo Díaz

“It has not yet been determined how many species will be identified with
paleontological study protocols, but, in the first observations, this variety
of footprints can expand our knowledge about many aspects of dinosaurs in
Mexico, such as locomotion, the direction of their gait and, with that, the
coexistence between species, behavior and morphology,” the archaeologist Punzo
Díaz added.

![INAH specialists examining the footprints at the
site](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/apatzingan-
dinosaur-tracks-03.jpg)Specialists went to the site and identified tracks of
two carnivorous theropods, others similar to those of raptors, and duck-billed
dinosaurs. Photo: INAH

Paleontologist Cervantes Barriga comments that in Michoacán there are
precedents of this type of footprints at three sites: Playa Azul, in Lázaro
Cárdenas; El Aguaje, in Aguililla, and the border of Tiquicheo and Tuzantla.
Now, this point in Apatzingán would be the fourth. **In Mexico there are just
over 30 sites with dinosaur ichnites registered with INAH** , located in the
states of Puebla, Coahuila, Oaxaca, Chihuahua, Sonora, Durango and Michoacán.
